title: AppImage first-launch desktop integration (writes to ~/.local/share)
decision: When Switchboard detects at startup that it is running inside an AppImage ($APPIMAGE env var set), it self-installs a .desktop entry to ~/.local/share/applications/switchboard.desktop and hicolor icon PNGs (sizes 16-512) to ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/*/apps/switchboard.png, then best-effort refreshes the desktop and icon caches. The Exec line points at the current $APPIMAGE path with --no-sandbox %U. The install is idempotent (skipped when the on-disk Exec already matches) and self-updating on version upgrades (path comparison re-writes when $APPIMAGE changes). A Preferences → Daemons → Desktop integration section exposes an explicit Uninstall action for reversibility. Failures are logged; the app continues to function without the integration.

context.task_description: On Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME (Wayland), the dock/app-grid resolves window icons via .desktop entries matched to app_id, not via BrowserWindow.icon (Wayland has no per-window icon protocol). AppImages do not install a .desktop entry on their own, so the dock falls back to the generic Electron gear icon. Sprint 19 embedded BrowserWindow.icon (rc.10) but that only helps on X11. Live-test on rc.10 confirmed the generic icon still shows on Wayland.
assumptions: Users prefer one packaging format across distros; AppImage is that format going forward (rc.12 will retire .deb + snap targets)
Writing to ~/.local/share is standard practice for third-party apps; AppImageLauncher / appimaged do the same

options.label: AppImage self-install of .desktop + icons on first launch
options.description: App writes to ~/.local/share/{applications,icons/hicolor/*/apps} on startup when $APPIMAGE is set; idempotent by Exec= comparison; explicit Preferences uninstall. Universal across distros. Standard AppImage integration pattern.

options.label: Keep multiple packaging targets (.deb + .snap + AppImage) and instruct users to pick
options.description: Preserves distro-native integration but forces the user to make a distribution choice and multiplies build/verification surface. Rejected: user preference is a single mechanism.

options.label: Require AppImageLauncher (third-party tool) for integration
options.description: Cleanest UX when the tool is installed but forces a hard dependency the user cannot control. Rejected: adds a mandatory install step.

rationale: AppImages are a single-file cross-distro format but come without desktop integration on their own. The self-install pattern is well-established (used by appimaged, AppImageUpdate, and many packaged tools), reversible via the Preferences Uninstall action, and updates itself when the AppImage path changes. Uniform --no-sandbox in the Exec line handles Ubuntu 24.04's unprivileged-user-namespace restriction while trading off the Chromium sandbox layer (acceptable given the app runs its own trusted daemon and the security model already relies on contextIsolation + IPC validation for the renderer).

risk.rollback: Delete src/main/desktop-install.ts and the wiring in main.ts/ipc-handlers.ts/preload.ts; remove the DesktopIntegrationSection from PreferencesModal.tsx. The written .desktop entry and icons persist until the user runs the Uninstall action or manually deletes them from ~/.local/share/.

outcome.notes: rc.11 in flight. Live verification on Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME Wayland required to confirm icon resolves in dock and app grid.
